title: Make it obvious
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Where could you place a cue so you cannot miss it?

A student said: the first thing is to make it obvious. Time and location are two obvious ways to do it. For example: in the morning, when I brush my teeth, I will do a quick reflection right after that. So you have an immediate cue.
Jose said we can also call these triggers. He said the book talks about choice architecture, the design of the choices around you.

Jose said that an office triggers people: I have to sit at my desk, pick up the phone, write emails. He said that is a reason people work in an office, and a leader who wants everyone in the office wants to control the choice architecture.
He said that in a supermarket, what is at eye level appeals more than what is at your feet, so placing things in strategic positions makes the choice more likely.
He said you can argue that habits change depending on the environment, the invisible hand that shapes human behavior: every habit is somehow context dependent.
What is at eye level in your day, and what do you want to be?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a habit you want to start.
Write the time and the place you will do it.
Write the thing that comes right before it.
Write what you could put at eye level.
Write what you could move out of sight.

check.q: What did a student say are two obvious ways to make a habit obvious?
What did Jose call the design of the choices around you?
What did Jose say about a supermarket?
choices: Things at eye level appeal more

recap: Make the cue obvious. Design the choices around you.
